Stacks on [#34531](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/34531)
. After that PR the binary was correct but wasteful: if  
any CJS package or native addon survived bundling, we shipped the entire  
resolved npm tree. The lodash hello-world embedded 11.6 MB of payload;  
`@node-rs/crc32` embedded 10.6 MB.

This reuses the data the path-rewriter already has. Every absolute path  
it rewrote in the bundle, and in each worker bundle, is the runtime  
require target of a CJS module reachable from the entrypoint. The binary  
writer maps each back to its owning npm package by longest-prefix folder  
match, walks the dependency closure so packages required transitively at  
runtime stay too, and embeds only those `<.deno>/<id>/node_modules/`  
directories.

Embedding the `<id>/node_modules/` parent rather than the canonical  
package folder is load-bearing for the NAPI-RS layout: the deno linker  
creates sibling symlinks for platform-specific optional packages  
(`@node-rs/crc32-darwin-arm64` lives as a symlink next to  
`@node-rs/crc32`), and walking just the canonical folder leaves those  
out, so the require chain breaks at the platform binary.

Not every rewritten path lives inside a node\_modules tree. The  
CJS-from-ESM wrapper also externalizes local project files imported from  
ESM (a sibling .cjs/.js required at runtime) into  
`require2(__internalResolveBundlePath("..."))` rather than inlining  
them. npm packages survive because their tree is embedded, but local  
files were never embedded, so the compiled binary failed at runtime with  
"Cannot find module". Referenced paths outside any node\_modules tree are  
treated as local files and added to the compile include set, so they  
ship in the VFS at their real path, which is where  
`__internalResolveBundlePath` looks at runtime. Covered by the  
`local_cjs_file` spec test.

Real reductions on the same fixtures from the earlier bundle PRs:

*   lodash hello-world: 11.62 MB to 1.45 MB embedded payload (~8x)
*   `@node-rs/crc32` hello-world: 10.62 MB to 468 KB embedded payload (~23x)
*   chalk hello-world (pure ESM): unchanged at 17 KB

The full resolution snapshot still ships in metadata so node-module  
resolution by name works at runtime; only the on-disk content shrinks.  
BYONM keeps the prior whole-tree behavior, since precise scoping there  
needs workspace-layout awareness and is left to a follow-up. Because  
package collection only returns None for BYONM (already handled on its  
own resolver arm), the managed arm uses a let-else with an unreachable  
invariant rather than a dead whole-tree fallback.

Stacks on top of [#34527](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/34527)
. Two things to make \`compile --bundle\` usable
with anything beyond pure-ESM trees.

First, the bundler's CJS-from-ESM wrapper hardcodes the absolute path of
each CJS module it imports. At runtime the VFS is mounted at a temp dir
under $TMPDIR, so those paths miss. Rewrite each literal in the bundle
output to a runtime-relative resolution against \`import.meta.url\` so it
survives relocation.

Second, when those rewritten requires hit something at runtime — either
a CJS dep loaded through the wrapper or a \`.node\` native addon — the
npm tree has to ship in the binary. Detect both signals (the rewrite
fired; or \`find\_native\_addon\_packages\` found a package with a \`.node\`
in the resolved snapshot) and embed the full snapshot in that case.
Pure-ESM bundles still skip everything npm and stay tiny.

Tested with chalk (pure ESM, ~17 KB user payload), lodash (CJS, full
npm), and \`@node-rs/crc32\` (native addon, full npm — addon loads and
runs). Spec test under \`tests/specs/compile/bundle/native\_addon/\`
exercises the addon path against the local \`@denotest/node-addon\`
fixture.

Testing the full stack (34527 → 34529 → 34531 → 34532, plus 34533 merged on top) against pi-coding-agent surfaced one remaining blocker that's distinct from the tslib `__toESM` interop bug.

`deno compile --bundle` fails with a `Parse error` whenever the entry's static import graph reaches an ESM file that default-imports a `.cjs` specifier. `deno run` and standalone `deno bundle` both accept it.

2-file minimal repro
--------------------

```shell
$ cat foo.cjs
module.exports = function() { return 42; };

$ cat entry.mjs
import f from "./foo.cjs";
console.log(f());

$ deno run entry.mjs                   # 42
$ deno bundle entry.mjs                # Bundled 2 modules → 1.52 KB
$ deno compile --bundle entry.mjs
Warning deno compile --bundle is experimental and may change.
error: Parse error
    at file:///private/tmp/cjs-import/entry.mjs:1:14
error: bundling failed
```

Toggle: rename `foo.cjs` → `foo.js`, change the import to match, and `deno compile --bundle` succeeds. Only the `.cjs` extension on the imported specifier flips the behavior.

Where the error originates
--------------------------

The error comes from `BundleLoadErrorKind::Parse(#[from] deno_ast::ParseDiagnostic)` — i.e. the `deno_ast::parse_program_with_post_process` call in `apply_transform` at `cli/tools/bundle/mod.rs:1734`. That transform is unique to the `--bundle`\-for-compile path (it injects `import.meta.main`); standalone `deno bundle` doesn't run it, which is why the same input bundles fine there.

Why it matters for real apps
----------------------------

In pi-coding-agent the same parse error surfaces transitively because [jiti](https://github.com/unjs/jiti)
 ships an ESM wrapper (`jiti.mjs`) that default-imports its CJS dist:

```js
// node_modules/.deno/jiti@2.7.0/node_modules/jiti/lib/jiti.mjs
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import _createJiti from "../dist/jiti.cjs";       // ← parse error here
import _babelTransform from "../dist/babel.cjs";
```

Jiti is fairly widely deployed (its bun-compiled-binary path uses this exact shape; the comment in the source confirms), so anything that transitively depends on jiti will hit this. A 4-line `package.json` with just `"dependencies": { "jiti": "^2" }` + `import jiti from "jiti"` reproduces.

What works on this stack
------------------------

For the record, on a 1-package tslib repro the merged stack now succeeds end-to-end:

    deno compile --allow-read --node-modules-dir=auto --bundle --output bin entry.mjs
    ./bin
    → __extends: function, __assign: function
    

97 KB embedded payload, 75 MB binary. So [#34533](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/34533)
 lands the `__toESM` fix and the embed-scope work in this PR (34532) keeps the binary tight. The remaining gap is the `.cjs`\-in-static-imports case in the deno\_ast transform path.

After that PR the binary was correct but wasteful: if
any CJS package or native addon survived bundling, we shipped the entire
resolved npm tree. The lodash hello-world embedded 11.6 MB of payload;
\`@node-rs/crc32\` embedded 10.6 MB.

This reuses the data the path-rewriter already has. Every absolute path
it rewrote in the bundle, and in each worker bundle, is the runtime
require target of a CJS module reachable from the entrypoint. The binary
writer maps each back to its owning npm package by longest-prefix folder
match, walks the dependency closure so packages required transitively at
runtime stay too, and embeds only those \`<.deno>/<id>/node\_modules/\`
directories.

Embedding the \`<id>/node\_modules/\` parent rather than the canonical
package folder is load-bearing for the NAPI-RS layout: the deno linker
creates sibling symlinks for platform-specific optional packages
(\`@node-rs/crc32-darwin-arm64\` lives as a symlink next to
\`@node-rs/crc32\`), and walking just the canonical folder leaves those
out, so the require chain breaks at the platform binary.

Not every rewritten path lives inside a node\_modules tree. The
CJS-from-ESM wrapper also externalizes local project files imported from
ESM (a sibling .cjs/.js required at runtime) into
\`require2(\_\_internalResolveBundlePath("..."))\` rather than inlining
them. npm packages survive because their tree is embedded, but local
files were never embedded, so the compiled binary failed at runtime with
"Cannot find module". Referenced paths outside any node\_modules tree are
treated as local files and added to the compile include set, so they
ship in the VFS at their real path, which is where
\`\_\_internalResolveBundlePath\` looks at runtime. Covered by the
\`local\_cjs\_file\` spec test.

Real reductions on the same fixtures from the earlier bundle PRs:

- lodash hello-world: 11.62 MB to 1.45 MB embedded payload (~8x)
- \`@node-rs/crc32\` hello-world: 10.62 MB to 468 KB embedded payload
(~23x)
- chalk hello-world (pure ESM): unchanged at 17 KB

The full resolution snapshot still ships in metadata so node-module
resolution by name works at runtime; only the on-disk content shrinks.
BYONM keeps the prior whole-tree behavior, since precise scoping there
needs workspace-layout awareness and is left to a follow-up. Because
package collection only returns None for BYONM (already handled on its
own resolver arm), the managed arm uses a let-else with an unreachable
invariant rather than a dead whole-tree fallback.
